bullets.title: STX: Monster beat + guide; consensus PT target raised sharply to ~$1,093
bullets.body: Seagate Q4 revenue $3.63B (+3.7% vs consensus), gross margin 52.7% (+170bps vs consensus), EPS $5.71 (+12% vs consensus). Q1 guidance EPS $7.30 is 25% above consensus; nearline supply largely allocated into CY28 with HAMR-driven ASP gains +20% sequentially. 82% of sell-side rates Buy with average PT raised 6.8% to $1,092; Barclays raised to $1,250, Mizuho to $1,090, Wells Fargo to $1,180. Morgan Stanley notes STX has beaten guidance by ~$0.70 for two consecutive quarters with FCF path to $8-10B/yr as density scales without meaningful capex.

bullets.title: META preview: Street expects $60.2B revenue, $7.19 EPS; capex/AI monetization the key swing factors
bullets.body: F2Q26 consensus is $60.2B revenue (+28% y/y), 80.4% gross margin, $7.19 EPS. Consensus capex expectation is $33.3B for the quarter and $134.6B for FY26 (guidance $125-145B); FY27 capex seen at $200-250B. Morgan Stanley and Citi both flag investors will focus on AI monetization signals, Muse/Watermelon model roadmaps, and whether capex is reiterated or raised. Credit markets are repricing AI risk with META CDS at record wides.

bullets.title: MSFT preview: Azure guided +39-40% y/y; FY27 capex seen at $240-260B; short interest at 11-yr high
bullets.body: Street expects Azure growth to accelerate modestly to 42-43% by Dec-Q. Capex guided ~$190B CY26 with market annualizing to $240-260B for FY27; Copilot seat adds of 6M+ expected. Separately, MSFT short interest hit its highest level since May 2015, and the UK CMA has opened a probe into subscription-plan marketing linked to Copilot price hikes.

bullets.title: AAPL F3Q26 preview: $109B revenue, $1.89 EPS; Services +14.6% y/y; AI strategy and iPhone ASPs in focus
bullets.body: Street expects F3Q26 revenue $109.0B vs $108.6B guidance midpoint, EPS $1.89, gross margin 48.0%. Services at $31.4B (+14.6% y/y) is decelerating from +16.3% prior. Key watches: iPhone demand elasticity from price increases, Siri/AI strategy update, China market dynamics. AAPL recently hit $5T market cap, surpassing NVDA, with NTM P/E ~36x above post-COVID peak.

bullets.title: VRT: -13% premarket on earnings; KLAC: -9.5% on miss; semis broadly under pressure
bullets.body: Vertiv fell 13% pre-market on its earnings report. KLA missed and fell 9.5%, with AMAT -3.3% and LRCX -2.8% in sympathy. Morgan Stanley notes KLAC's near-term results were underwhelming but is constructive on 2027 toward $190B+ WFE; Wolfe notes KLAC's CY26 systems revenue tracking inline with WFE at mid-20s% YoY growth. SOX index is down 25% from recent highs, fastest drawdown to zero members above 50-day MA on record.

bullets.title: NVDA/Hyperscaler CDS at record wides; B200 GPU spot rates +9% q/q; AI financing risk crystallizing
bullets.body: Cost of protecting NVDA debt against default surged to record CDS spread widening. Oracle and Coreweave CDS are deteriorating at an "alarming" pace per Torsten Slok data. B200 GPU rental rates are up 9% from Q2 and 22% above Q1. Goldman estimates ~$250B of hyperscaler capex will be debt-financed in 2026 (33% of total). HY credit reversed its AI overweight to underweight after AI credit returned 8.5% through June but lagged by -300bp in July.

bullets.title: Mag 7 positioning near 1-year lows; largest 3-day HF degrossing since Nov 2022
bullets.body: Prime brokerage data shows the three-day cumulative de-grossing (Fri-Tue) is the largest since November 2022 and largest for single names since March 2025. Global Info Tech saw the largest long selling on record since 2016 over the past three sessions. Mag 7 names were collectively net bought but positioning remains at the 6th and 4th percentiles on net exposure and long/short ratio, near 1-year lows.

bullets.title: TER: Strong Q2 beat-and-raise; record Memory revenue; Q3 guide above estimates
bullets.body: Teradyne Q2 revenue $1.33B vs FactSet $1.22B, EPS $2.47 vs $2.09. Q3 guidance revenue $1.2-1.3B ahead of estimates. Memory revenue up 104% y/y to a record; DDR and NAND robust through 2027. Networking TAM expected 15-20% CAGR mid-term; CPO test market seen at $300-700M by 2028. Stock was +14.1% in premarket.

bullets.title: ARM preview: CPU sales guidance update to $2B for FY28; datacenter royalties need to reach 19% of total
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley previews ARM with bullish datacenter tone but notes soft handset demand; UBS lowered PT to $360 citing weak smartphone backdrop. The key metric to watch is whether management updates CPU sales guidance for FY28 (currently ~$1B) and whether datacenter royalties are tracking toward 19% of total revenue needed to justify current valuation.

bullets.title: ADBE: FTC clears Topaz Labs acquisition; stock +$12.88 on news
bullets.body: The FTC granted antitrust clearance for Adobe's acquisition of Topaz Labs, an AI video/image enhancement company. The transaction was announced June 25 and is expected to close H2 2026. ADBE shares rose ~$12.88 on the news.

bullets.title: V: Clean Q3 beat; KeyBanc/Goldman raise PTs; July US volume +9%, strongest post-COVID
bullets.body: Visa Q3 EPS $3.32 vs $3.23 consensus, revenue +2% above estimates. July US payment volume growth of +9% is the strongest post-COVID reading. VAS (value-added services) grew +34% y/y. FY26 revenue guidance raised; NG EPS growth reaffirmed at mid-teens. KeyBanc raised PT to $425, Goldman to $438, BMO to $405; Citi raised PT to $440. 93% buy ratings with average PT $413.

bullets.title: BE: Q2 revenue >$1B (+166% y/y); FY26 guidance raised; sold off on execution/valuation concerns
bullets.body: Bloom Energy reported Q2 revenue above $1B for the first time, up 166% y/y; FY26 guidance was raised. Despite the beat, the stock sold off on valuation and execution concerns per Morgan Stanley. Stock was +10.1% in premarket after the initial reaction. Morgan Stanley's ESG team continues to favor BE as an AI infrastructure play.

bullets.title: SNAP Q2 preview: $1.54B revenue, 486.7M DAUs; options imply ~16% move
bullets.body: Street consensus for SNAP Q2 is $1.54B revenue (vs guidance $1.52-1.55B), EBITDA $192M, DAUs 486.7M, global ARPU $3.16. SNAP is up 21.5% since May earnings. Q3 consensus is $1.70B revenue with EBITDA $327M. Options imply a ~16.3% move; earnings scheduled after the close.

bullets.title: ON (onsemi): Q2 consensus $1.59B revenue, $0.71 EPS; options imply ~15% move; strong beat history
bullets.body: Onsemi Q2 consensus is $1.59B revenue (vs guidance $1.535-1.635B) and $0.71 EPS (vs guidance $0.65-0.77). The company has beaten revenue and EPS consensus in 18 of the past 20 quarters. Options imply a ~14.8% move. Q3 guidance is expected around $1.67B revenue / $0.83 EPS.

bullets.title: FTNT F2Q26 preview: $1,888M revenue, 80.2% gross margin; Services re-acceleration the key watch
bullets.body: Fortinet Street consensus for F2Q26 is $1,888M revenue, 80.2% gross margin, 34% operating margin, $0.75 EPS. Key investor focus: Services revenue re-acceleration, Product demand durability, AI/OT security performance, and 2H demand pull-forward risk. Morgan Stanley recently upgraded FTNT to Equal-Weight, noting no negative near-term catalyst.

bullets.title: CTSH: Q2 beat, raised FY26 EPS guidance to $5.70-$5.82; AI-led BPO driving growth
bullets.body: Cognizant Q2 revenue $5.48B matched consensus; EPS $1.37 vs $1.38. Financial services growth accelerating; clients shifting to productionizing AI. FY26 EPS raised to $5.70-$5.82 (prior $5.63-$5.77), with 8-10% growth. Trailing 12-month bookings $29.1B, up 5% y/y. Q3 revenue guidance $5.60-$5.68B is slightly below FactSet $5.70B.

bullets.title: SNOW, NET, PINS: Hedgeye flags all three in bullish signal-strength long list
bullets.body: Hedgeye's fractal momentum model lists Cloudflare (NET), Snowflake (SNOW), and Pinterest (PINS) among current long signal-strength positions on both TRADE and TREND durations. Separately, SNOW introduced Cortex AI Gateway this week and hit a new 52-week high of $283.70 (+29.7% over 52 weeks).

bullets.title: CHTR, GLW: PT cuts from multiple brokers; GLW -12% on earnings; CDS deteriorating
bullets.body: JP Morgan cut CHTR PT to $150 from $200. GLW fell ~12% on disappointing earnings; JPMorgan cut GLW PT to $170 from $200, Citi cut to $220 from $240, Barclays cut to $129. JP Morgan notes the long-term optical story for GLW remains intact. CDS spreads across tech broadly are widening with Oracle and Coreweave in a separate, worse category.

bullets.title: APP: Citi Buy with $710 PT; 2Q preview expects $1.94B revs, $1.64B EBITDA; eCommerce to drive >50% of growth by 2028
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on AppLovin with $710 PT ahead of 2Q results, expecting $1.94B revenue and $1.64B adj. EBITDA. eCommerce vertical expected to drive more than 50% of aggregate topline growth by 2028. The stock is described as the key application-layer beneficiary as semiconductor sentiment softens.

bullets.title: DIS: Citi cuts PT to $135; FY26 16% adj. EPS growth guide at risk from Entertainment underperformance
bullets.body: Citi lowered its Disney PT to $135, flagging risk to the FY26 guidance of 16%+ adj. EPS growth given Entertainment segment underperformance (Mandalorian, Moana) and elevated SVOD content spend. Wolfe Research is also hosting a webinar on whether state AG lawsuits against Paramount-Skydance create regulatory risk, with a Sept 30 closing deadline flagged as a pressure point.
